summary: Rogue River NF crow's nest in a 30-foot tree, built 1917; staffed into the 1920s; abandoned 1928 after a cupola went up on Dutchman's Peak. Present state unknown.

facts.design: crow's nest in the top of a 30-foot tree, with a cabin nearby
facts.status_note: Fire Lookout Association list says Abandoned; firelookout.com, undated, says the crow's nest was still there when written; no later source found
facts.agency_note: Sources of 1916 and 1924 call it the Crater National Forest; renamed Rogue River National Forest in July 1932

events.note: 1916 report recommended a 100-foot steel tower that would need 125 trees felled; the crow's nest was built instead in 1917

corrections.proposed: omit; the lookout was a crow's nest in the top of a 30-foot tree (tree height, not nest height)
corrections.why: 30.5 m (100 ft) matches the 1916 recommendation for a 100-foot steel tower that would have required felling 125 trees; the structure built in 1917 was a crow's nest in a 30-foot tree
The Fire Lookout Association list says Abandoned, not removed, and firelookout.com says the crow's nest was still there when written; no later source describes the site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The association list (Abandoned) and the undated firelookout.com note ('still there') disagree; neither is dated to today, so the record keeps status unknown rather than gone or standing.
firelookout.com says log cabin; Forest Lookouts quotes the 1917 record as a shake-sided cabin. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Staffing years come from the personnel tables in the Rogue River history, dated by the nearest year heading above each table; the years are inferred from those headings. A 1944 Medford Mail Tribune item on the Forest Lookouts page gives the same guard and the same date (September 5) as 1924 but a different year; left out as likely an error on the page. The geocaching page for GC34T92 did not load. Present condition is unverified; a recent visit or a Forest Service record would settle it. Fact-check 2026-10-10: removed the earlier 'Forest Service set up' attribution (no cited page names who built the lookout); added the 1922 Alex Schichtl listing and the Crater National Forest naming with the July 1932 rename.
